growth_story.headline: Georgia's income per person collapsed after independence, surged after the 2003 reforms, and has grown 5.0 percent a year since 2008 to a new high in 2025.
growth_story.arc: In 1990–1997 growth in income per person averaged -10.6 percent a year, as independence brought civil war, secessionist conflicts and hyperinflation; a stabilization program in 1994–96 brought growth back before the era ended. In 1998–2007 growth averaged 7.9 percent a year, held back at first by corruption and an energy crisis and then lifted by the reforms that followed the 2003 Rose Revolution, reaching 13.2 in 2007. Since 2008 growth has averaged 5.0 percent a year: the August 2008 war with Russia and the global financial crisis pushed it to -2.8 in 2009, and the pandemic pushed it to -6.4 in 2020. Recovering tourism, and then a surge of migrants, money and transit trade after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, lifted growth to 11.1 in 2021 and 10.8 in 2022. Growth over 2016–2025 averaged 5.4 percent a year, a little below the 5.9 of 2006–2015, and income per person was at its highest level yet in 2025, though it passed its 1985 level only in 2018.

threads.title: Collapse, then reform
threads.text: After independence in 1991, civil war, breakaway regions and hyperinflation brought a sharp and long fall in output. Corruption, poor management and an energy crisis then held the economy back until the 2003 Rose Revolution brought a fast reform program and rapid growth.

citations.quote: Civil war, secessionist movements, and economic crises resulted in a sharp and protracted fall in output and hyperinflation in the immediate post-independence years.

citations.title: Georgia Country Assistance Evaluation, 1993-2007 (IEG Fast Track Brief)
citations.quote: the government failed to overcome problems arising notably from economic mismanagement and widespread corruption, leading to poor public services, a deepening energy crisis

citations.title: Georgia Country Assistance Evaluation, 1993-2007 (IEG Fast Track Brief)
citations.quote: After the November 2003 Rose Revolution, the new government executed an ambitious reform program that quickly produced results

threads.title: War and crisis in 2008
threads.text: The August 2008 war with Russia and the global financial crisis hit at the same time. Bank deposits fled and credit was squeezed. In the data, 2008 opens the slower era that runs to today.

citations.title: Georgia: 2011 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 11/87)
citations.quote: The government moved forcefully to counter the economic impact of the August 2008 conflict with Russia and global financial crisis

citations.title: Georgia: 2011 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 11/87)
citations.quote: Monetary and prudential policy easing was, however, unable to prevent a sharp credit squeeze.

citations.title: Georgia: 2011 Article IV Consultation—Staff Report (IMF Country Report No. 11/87)
citations.quote: The confidence shock triggered by the war and subsequent political instability led to a 29 percent loss of deposits (exchange rate adjusted)

threads.title: Wartime inflows of people and money
threads.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine brought a surge of migrants, money and transit trade through Georgia. The boom they started in information technology, transport and education services still carries growth.

citations.title: Georgia: 2024 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Georgia (IMF Country Report No. 24/135)
citations.quote: a surge in immigration, financial inflows, and transit trade triggered by Russia’s war in Ukraine have boosted GDP growth and fiscal revenues

citations.title: Georgia: 2026 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Georgia (IMF Country Report No. 26/133)
citations.quote: activity has been driven by continued strength in information and communication technology (ICT), transport, and education services, initially boosted by financial and migrant inflows

threads.title: A stalled path to Europe
threads.text: Talks on joining the European Union are on hold, and the sources describe episodes of civil unrest and a slower pace of reform. They list this political strain among the risks to growth in the years ahead.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Georgia
citations.quote: Reform momentum has moderated amid episodes of civil unrest, and the suspension of European Union accession talks until 2028.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Georgia
citations.quote: domestic political polarization, suspended European Union accession negotiations, and slow structural reforms pose medium-term risks

citations.title: Georgia: 2026 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Georgia (IMF Country Report No. 26/133)
citations.quote: Relations with the EU remain strained, with the EU’s 2025 Enlargement Report indicating accession is on hold.

threads.title: Emigration and scarce good jobs
threads.text: A 2022 World Bank study found the population smaller than at the start of the century, mostly because people left, and ageing. Even after years of fast growth, unemployment stays high, above all among the young.

citations.title: Georgia Country Economic Memorandum Chapter 1: Understanding Georgia’s Growth
citations.quote: is down by a full 7.7 percent compared to the start of this century (Box 1). This is largely due to outward migration

citations.title: Georgia Country Economic Memorandum Chapter 1: Understanding Georgia’s Growth
citations.quote: Georgia has a small, and aging, population, with a declining rate of participation in the labor market.

citations.title: Georgia: 2026 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Georgia (IMF Country Report No. 26/133)
citations.quote: Unemployment remains structurally high, particularly among youth (Figure 1), reflecting persistent skill mismatches and weak work incentives amid low wages

since_last_year.text: Growth stayed strong into 2026, carried by household spending and credit, but higher energy prices pushed inflation back up and the war in the Middle East hit tourism. In the data, growth in income per person slowed to 4.1 in 2025 from 6.9 in 2024.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Georgia
citations.quote: Georgia’s economy entered 2026 with strong momentum, as robust consumption and credit supported broad-based growth

citations.title: Georgia: 2026 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Georgia (IMF Country Report No. 26/133)
citations.quote: Real GDP expanded by 7.5 percent in 2025 and remained strong in early 2026, while inflation rose above target due to higher energy prices

citations.title: Georgia: 2026 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Georgia (IMF Country Report No. 26/133)
citations.quote: Economic activity remained firm in early 2026, with the impact from the Middle East war largely confined to tourism.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe 2024 and 2025 as boom years for the whole economy, but in the data income per person grew 6.9 in 2024 and only 4.1 in 2025, well below the economy-wide rates the sources report. The gap implies a rising population count in the data; the sources describe a surge in immigration after 2022 but do not say how much of the gap it explains.
